clue.text: Youngster forever safe when accompanied by father, note

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A child is kept safe whenever Dad is around, plus a reminder note.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old British underworld slang, as in a safe-cracker being a 'peterman'.
explanation.definitionFit: J.M. Barrie's hero is the boy who never grows up, staying a child for ever.

clue.text: Turned up with fizzy drink, last of wine kept for later

indicators.note: Turned here means turned over, so the letters of up are read the other way

parts.note: tonic is a fizzy mixer

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone arrived with a sparkling drink, the last of the wine saved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Put on ice is an idiom for postponing something, setting it aside to deal with later.

clue.text: Elevated site overlooking Crete sadly inaccessible to most people

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: the tops are high places, the elevated ground

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters of Crete are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hilltop above Crete, regrettably closed to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-secret information is classified, kept from all but a few with clearance.

clue.text: Some brat, typically grumpy

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spoilt child is, as a rule, bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: A burden directors must shoulder everywhere

indicators.note: in a down clue, carrying something on the shoulders puts it on top, so the burden sits above the directors

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden
the board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: Company directors must bear the weight of responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board is an idiom meaning applying to everyone or everything, all over.

clue.text: Mind job, etc, being reorganised

indicators.note: being reorganised says the letters of the words before are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A brain-teasing task and the like is being restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'Do you mind?'
explanation.definitionFit: To mind something is to dislike it or protest, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: British PM once restraining a cross, formidable woman

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the former prime minister contains the other letters

parts.note: Clement Attlee was UK Prime Minister 1945-51
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A former British prime minister holds back an angry, imposing woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleaxe is an informal term for a domineering, aggressive older woman.

clue.text: Chopping head off oil baron

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: hewing is chopping, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Decapitating a petroleum tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: J.R. Ewing is the oil tycoon of the US TV soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ewing family of Dallas made their fortune in Texas oil, J.R. being its scheming head.

clue.text: A number proceeded through outskirts of Tenby

indicators.note: through puts the word for proceeded between the outer letters
outskirts of means the outer letters of the town's name

parts.note: went means proceeded

explanation.surface: A bus went through the edges of Tenby, a Welsh seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a cardinal number, two tens.

clue.text: Pet dog ran with red ball thrown round middle of woods

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters surround the middle letter
thrown suggests things scattered, so these letters are jumbled
middle of means the central letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A family dog chases a red ball thrown among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet dog' wants to be the definition, but 'dog' is part of the anagram fodder with RAN and RED BALL, around the O at the centre of 'woods'.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of retriever is one of the most popular family companions.

clue.text: Barman prepared repast after very little time

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, and a single letter is very little of it

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of repast are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A bartender made a meal in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is someone who draws beer from the tap in a pub, an old word for a barman.

clue.text: Giant sounds sadder than everyone else, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say? marks a playful spoken pun on the words before

parts.note: someone who sighs more than everybody else could be said to out-sigh them

explanation.surface: A giant seems the gloomiest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: To out-sigh everyone is to sound sadder than all of them; spoken, that gives the word meaning extra large.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsize describes something unusually large, as giant does in its adjective sense.

clue.text: Poor Edward, gripped by recurring desire

indicators.note: gripped by puts Edward's short form inside the other piece
recurring here means coming back, so the word for desire is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Poor Edward is in the grip of a craving that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurring' turns YEN into NEY, which then holds ED.
explanation.definitionFit: The needy are those in want, a synonym of poor in its sense of lacking money.

clue.text: Accessory on car one's reversed near entrance

indicators.note: near says the first piece sits next to the second
reversed means the letters of one's are read in the other direction

parts.note: one's is read as I'S, one being I, giving I and S
to entrance someone is to delight them, the verb

explanation.surface: A car part sits back to front beside the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (stress on the second syllable), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp at the front corner of a vehicle, one of its fittings.

clue.text: Position in rest home attracted Anne in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests a loose version of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a retirement home was drawn to Anne, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A post in a residential home is a job looking after the elderly residents there.

clue.text: Cost of entry varies, Simon said

indicators.note: varies means changes, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Simon says ticket prices change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a link, but it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the fee charged to get in, as in an admission price.

clue.text: Child actor — about ten — in London area

indicators.note: about means the child and actor go round the number

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: A child performer of roughly ten in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottenham is a district of north London, home of the football club Spurs.

clue.text: Ordinary worker's eaten banana

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed, so the worker goes inside the word for ordinary

parts.note: plain means ordinary
worker's reads as worker is; an ant is a worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: An ordinary labourer has had a banana.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy kind of banana usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Moody office worker taking ages with one sort of arithmetic

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an era is a long period, ages
mental arithmetic is done in the head

explanation.surface: A sulky clerk spends ages doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperamental has unpredictable changes of mood, a synonym of moody.

clue.text: I transport American high-flyer

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone moves a high-achieving American.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings, literally flying high.

clue.text: Greek island to ancient city? That encompasses satisfactory type of holiday

indicators.note: encompasses means surrounds, so the Greek island holds the word for satisfactory

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
OK means satisfactory
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in crosswords

explanation.surface: A travel itinerary from a Greek island to an ancient city, acceptable to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' is a link pointing back to the island, which takes in OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cook's tour, after Thomas Cook's travel company, is a quick sightseeing trip taking in many places.

clue.text: Old and new song being broadcast

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Old and new songs are playing on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: On air is the broadcasting phrase for a programme going out live.

clue.text: He ruled Thebes a long time after King Charles

indicators.note: after puts the long period following the king's initials

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A historical note: a Theban ruler reigned ages after King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Creon is the king of Thebes in Sophocles' Antigone and Oedipus plays.

clue.text: Breeding shown by Conservative female

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A Tory woman displays her good upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Class can mean refinement or good breeding, as in 'she has real class'.

clue.text: More willing to perish in tower

indicators.note: in puts the word for perish inside the word for tower

parts.note: to tower is to rise high, to rear up
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Someone keener to meet their end inside a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is the verb meaning to rise, REAR, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready in its sense of willing or inclined.

clue.text: Children absorbed by play money, once

indicators.note: absorbed by means the children's letters go inside the word for play

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: Kids engrossed in a play about money, once upon a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was Greece's currency until the euro replaced it in 2002, so former money.

clue.text: Polish rabbi enters holy place

indicators.note: enters says the rabbi's letter goes inside the word for polish

parts.note: to shine shoes is to polish them

explanation.surface: A rabbi from Poland walks into a sacred building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a sacred site devoted to a saint or deity.

clue.text: Postgraduate close to exasperation, meeting cheeky young student

parts.note: fresh can mean impudent or cheeky
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a postgraduate

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A graduate student, near the end of their tether, meets an insolent undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a first-year student at college or university.
